newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods--Midcontinent gasoline grows tighter.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods--Midcontinent gasoline grows tighter.

text.p: Midcontinent spot gasoline markets appeared to be feeding off some of the fire in NYMEX, Gulf Coast and New York Harbor markets amid declining inventories in the Williams Pipeline system, traders said.

Differentials in Gulf and New York Harbor markets quieted largely due to the fireworks on NYMEX, which appeared to be far from over with markets rife with talk of some sort of squeeze play emerging on NYMEX ahead of the August expiry.

On the NYMEX, August gasoline was again surging ahead of the close, with August unleaded up by 3.28 to 69.70 cents a gallon. August heat, along for the ride, but relatively staid, was up by 1.04 cents to 55.35 cents a gallon.
MIDCONTINENT
"It's a bit 'fumey'", said one trader referring to gasoline inventories in the Williams Pipeline that are down to a relatively low 18 day supply.

Activity was a bit subdued however, particularly with the end of the month that had Group Three traders mostly interested in closing their books on July, though the odd distressed deals were getting done.

In the Group, the illiquid prompt July market for unleaded actually weakened, while the August market firmed amid unconfirmed reports early August barrels traded at 3.10 over September NYMEX on a relatively distressed basis.
Despite the near-term strength seen in the midcontinent, traders stressed that it was based on a homegrown version of the solid demand nationwide.
But the move lacked the depth of strength in Houston or New York where upside price action has been predicatated on a small but consequential number of processing problems on the refining front.
With the exception of a fire at a small refiner in Kansas last week, refiners have been remarkably free of production difficulties in the midcontinent so far this summer.
Distillates in both markets continued to be exceedingly quiet on the differential front.
NEW YORK HARBOR

Prompt conventional M2 gasoline differentials grew downright foggy by the time of the NYMEX close, with assessments ranging anywhere from 2.00 to 3.50 cents under August futures or anywhere from unchanged to a cent weaker than as of late Tuesday.
Reformulated A2 gasoline differentials, refusing to give up any of their recent gains, continued to expand in fact, with barrels heard getting done at 3.50 cents over the August.
Players attributed much of the strength to the shutdown of Tosco Bayway's catalytic cracking unit Wednesday, though rumors had circulated earlier in the week that unit be shut.
U.S. GULF
Activity on the U.S. Gulf Coast remained quiet Wednesday afternoon, muffled by the sharp rise in NYMEX gasoline futures that placed many traders on the sidelines.
"With the Merc up so much everyone is sitting back watching it very closely," said a Gulf trader.

Prices for M1-conventional unleaded gasoline, however, remained strong. Prompt, now the back 22nd-cycle for Colonial Pipeline delivery, M1 grade traded at 1.15 cents over the September futures and the range was pegged 1.00/1.40 cents over the print.
The front 22nd cycle had its scheduling deadline yesterday, closing sharply higher to offers at 2.00 cents.
A1-grade regular reformulated gasoline and the "D1" and "V1"- grade gasolines also remained high but trade was quiet.
"Those grades will remain lofty until MTBE comes down," said a Gulf trader, refering to the recent high values of the gasoline additive.
Meanwhile, there were unconfirmed rumors that Exxon Corp will bring back up its 110,000-barrel-per-day fluid catalytic cracking unit on Wednesday. It was downed on Monday by lightning.
Exxon said Wednesday morning the unit was still down but should be operational soon.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 8591 1620
